feed.title: Py Internals
feed.subtitle: An open-source, interactive Python course that shows what your code does in memory.

entry.title: Session 08: Exceptions, Tracebacks & Context Managers
entry.summary: What raise does to the call stack, how to read a traceback, why finally runs past a return, what with calls for you and how exceptions chain with from.

entry.title: Session 07: The GIL & Concurrency
entry.summary: Why CPython has a global interpreter lock, why it doesn't make your code thread-safe, and when threads, multiprocessing or asyncio actually help.

entry.title: Session 06: Decorators
entry.summary: A decorator is one line of assignment. See the wrapper, the closure cell that keeps your function alive, functools.wraps, decorator factories and stacking.

entry.title: Session 04: Classes & Objects
entry.summary: What self really is, where attributes live, how bound methods work, why class attributes are shared and how inheritance is just a longer lookup.

entry.title: Session 05: Iterators & Generators
entry.summary: How a for loop uses iter and next, what StopIteration does, how yield pauses a frame and what lazy evaluation costs in memory compared with a list.

entry.title: Session 03: Lists, Dicts & References
entry.summary: Why b = a shares a list, what a shallow copy really copies, how deepcopy differs, and why passing a dict to a function can change the caller's data.

entry.title: Session 02: Functions, Scope & the Call Stack
entry.summary: Watch a call frame appear and disappear. Local scope, LEGB lookup, arguments passed by reference, closures with real cells and the mutable default trap.

entry.title: Session 01: Variables & Mutability
entry.summary: See what x = 42 really does in memory. Names, objects, id(), aliasing, mutation versus rebinding and reference counting, animated one step at a time.
